title: Qiwu: Exploiting Ciphertext-Level SIMD Parallelism in Homomorphic Encryption Programs
problem: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) with CKKS scheme enables secure computation on encrypted data, but reduction operations create large bubbles (gaps) in intermediate ciphertexts that waste computational resources despite plaintext-level SIMD packing.
motivation: As secure cloud computing demands grow, improving FHE performance is critical; better resource utilization of packed ciphertexts directly translates to faster encrypted computation and more practical secure offloading.
method: Qiwu performs ciphertext-level vectorization by fusing multiple ciphertexts containing bubbles to eliminate gaps in output ciphertexts. A DSL specifies zero bubbles in inputs and nonzero bubbles in outputs; data-flow analysis tracks bubble patterns and a cost-benefit assessment guides fusion decisions.
key_novelty: Introducing ciphertext-level fusion for bubble elimination in FHE programs, complementing plaintext-level SIMD parallelism.
contributions: A ciphertext-level vectorization approach (Qiwu) for fusing multiple ciphertexts to eliminate bubbles
A DSL for specifying bubble patterns and a data-flow analysis for tracking them
Implementation in an existing FHE compiler with speedups up to 18.0x on CPUs (geometric mean 3.4x) vs state-of-the-art plaintext-only approaches
baselines: State-of-the-art FHE compiler exploiting only plaintext-level parallelism
limitations: Evaluation limited to 4 applications (3 ML, 1 kernel) and 3 kernels; GPU performance and scalability to larger programs not discussed.
primary_theme: Ciphertext-level fusion for FHE bubble elimination
